questions.stem: What does the abbreviation SIMD stand for?
options: Single Instruction Stream and Single Data Stream
Single Instruction Stream and Multiple Data Stream
Multiple Instruction Stream and Single Data Stream
Multiple Instruction Stream and Multiple Data Stream
Sequential Instruction and Multiple Disk
questions.explanation: SIMD is Single Instruction Stream and Multiple Data Stream: one instruction is applied to many data elements in parallel.

questions.stem: What does the abbreviation MISD stand for?
options: Multiple Instruction Stream and Multiple Data Stream
Multiple Index and Single Disk
Single Instruction Stream and Multiple Data Stream
Multiple Instruction Stream and Single Data Stream
Multi-core Instruction Set Design
questions.explanation: MISD is Multiple Instruction Stream and Single Data Stream: many instructions are sent to read the same piece of information.

questions.stem: What is a CPU core built of?
options: Billions of microscopic transistors that process instructions
A single large transistor
A block of hard-disk storage
A set of network cables
Several pages of stored data
questions.explanation: A CPU core is built of billions of microscopic transistors that process the instructions passed to it.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of cores required to handle multiple instructions in parallel?
options: One
Two
Four
Eight
Sixteen
questions.explanation: One instruction is handled by one core, so multitasking or parallel instructions require a minimum of two cores.

questions.stem: In the analogy of finding every letter 'A' written on a page, how does SISD behave?
options: It reads all the letters at once and returns them together
It sends several instructions in parallel
It reads and returns each 'A' one by one, sequentially, like a traditional human reader
It reads 'A' and 'B' at the same time
It skips letters it has already seen
questions.explanation: SISD works like a human reading one letter or word at a time, so each 'A' is read and returned sequentially, which is slow for large data.

questions.stem: Which problem of SISD does SIMD solve?
options: The inability to process instructions from more than one user
The need to move data on floppy drives
The lack of security parameters on queries
The limited size of the hard disk
The need to read each letter or word one by one
questions.explanation: SIMD processes in parallel: given one instruction to find the letter 'A', it reads all the 'A's at once and returns them much more quickly than SISD.

options: One instruction reading one data element at a time
One instruction reading many data elements in parallel
Many instructions reading the same data element one by one
Data being copied from one hard disk to another
Multiple instructions processed in parallel to read multiple data elements, such as all the 'A's and all the 'B's
questions.explanation: MIMD lets several instructions or queries run in parallel to read different sets of information, for example all the 'A's along with all the 'B's.

questions.stem: In MISD, how are hundreds of instructions to read the same letter 'A' processed?
options: One by one, sequentially, which takes a lot of time
All at once on a single core
By splitting the page across nodes
By caching the first result and reusing it
By rejecting all but the first instruction
questions.explanation: With MISD, multiple instructions are sent to read the same piece of information but each instruction is processed sequentially, so many instructions take a long time.

questions.stem: On what do all the multi-instruction or multi-data reads ultimately depend?
options: The version of the query language
The speed of the network connection
The size of the page being read
The number of cores available in the computer, server or node
The amount of free hard-disk space
questions.explanation: All parallel instruction or data processing is bounded by the number of cores available in the machine, server or node.

questions.stem: How many types of instruction for pulling data are there in this classification?
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
Six
questions.explanation: There are four types: SISD, SIMD, MISD and MIMD.
